debris.notes: A dented slab of skin plating with the stringers still riveted to its back — the commonest thing in the low sky, and the piece a player learns the crushed-slot rule on.
A buckled length of lattice strut, five times the mass of the panels drifting beside it for twice the slots — the first place the size class, not the individual piece, becomes the decision.

A baled tangle of gold multilayer foil and its aluminium standoffs; it looks like it should weigh nothing and does not, which is the joke — the smalls in this band all cost about the same to haul, and the light run is a hold full of them rather than a hunt for the lightest one.

A burnt-out solid upper-stage casing with the throat plug still fused in — three of them is the greediest legal base hold in the band at 1095 kg, putting the ship at 2.2x its dry mass on a first-tier chute.
A snapped-off length of boom tubing with the mount flange still attached; cheap, plentiful, and light enough to string three at a time without the load fighting back.
A spidered pane of pressure glazing still bolted into its frame; the player's first lesson that a glinting piece cannot be crushed and hates a hard touchdown.
A rack of swollen cells bolted to a carrier plate; interchangeable with the band's other mediums on the scale, and a good early test of whether the hold or the chute gives out first.

A curved wedge of parabolic backing shell that catches the sun on a slow cycle; one of them eats four of a base hold's six slots for less than half the mass of a solid medium — the bulk-versus-density lesson, and no longer a free one on the way down.
Half a payload shroud, big as a shed and crane-cable only — visible in the low sky all game as a promise of what the winch will one day reach. Unreachable in the shipping slice.
A sealed drum of gyro and bearing, one crushed slot and startlingly dense in the hand — nearly three times a suborbital hull panel for the same slot, which is the band change made physical.

A hinged wing of cells with a fractured spar, glinting off the common clumps on its own faster orbit; the signature fragile piece of the slice, and mass-cheap for the four slots it never stops costing.
A ruptured titanium sphere, still smelling of hydrazine; one of four low-band mediums that weigh within three percent of each other, so which one you grab is a matter of what drifted closest.
A shielded box of flight computers wrenched free of its rack; compact, heavy for its size, and the low band's reliable filler.
A baffled optical head with its lens intact — a fragile piece light enough that a botched latch is survivable, and worth crossing a band-width of empty sky for if the touchdown can be kept soft.
A finned slab of coolant plumbing; broad and slow to stop, so it swings wide on every turn of a loaded string.

A machined ring of latches and seals, the heaviest single hand-tether in the shipping slice; two of them is 1110 kg on the line against a 110 kg suit, which is a deliberate two-trip-or-one decision rather than a fight with the jetpack.
A cast frame with three wheels still mounted; solid, forgiving, and the piece that teaches how a medium tows against a small.
A flared waveguide horn with its window unbroken; the fragile piece players learn technique on, because at this mass a mistimed latch strains the cable rather than shearing it.
A split-open habitat tank the size of a bus; crane-cable only and out of reach until the winch ships. Unreachable in the shipping slice.
The structural heart of a dead satellite, packed with harness and shielding; the high band's staple, and a quarter more mass per slot than the best the low band offers.

An empty isotope-generator cask of layered tungsten; one crushed slot and half a ton, and the only piece in the catalog that is alone in its band-class-fragility group — so it is free to be an outlier without dominating anything.
A full unfolded array wing, acres of cell and hinge; it glints from half a screen away and cannot be crushed at any tier.
A telescope barrel with its cold mirror still seated, orbiting well off the clumps at real relative speed; a patient approach or a torn-off magnet.
A stack of etched molybdenum accelerator grids still bolted into their steel mounting can — paper-thin optics inside a mass that is all housing, and priceless if the can never lands hard.
Four wheels on a common casting, still spinning slowly; the heaviest hand-tetherable piece in the game, and a pair of them rewrites the descent plan.
A niobium expansion nozzle, scorched blue at the throat; solid, forgiving, and the safe pick when the hold is already fragile-heavy.
A vacuum-sealed maser package on vibration mounts; small, glinting, rare enough that most runs never see one, and the single most demanding hand-tether in the game.
A furled gold-mesh dish on a deployable rib frame; bulky, uncrushable, and it fills a hold far faster than its mass suggests.
A whole communications payload rack sheared from its bus; unglamorous, enormously heavy, and the backbone of a profitable top-band run.
An interstage skirt with the separation ring still bolted on — crane-cable only, and the practice run for Mr. Armstrong's satellite above it. Unreachable in the shipping slice.

revision_notes: Concern 1 (flat class pricing makes the lightest piece in a group strictly dominant): agreed, and it is the correct reading of the Balancer's schema. If value depends only on band and size class, then two pieces sharing a band, a class and a fragile flag are priced identically and occupy identical slots, so mass is the only difference between them and less mass is always better. There is no clever mass assignment that fixes this — the only catalog in which no piece is strictly dominated is one where every such group is flat. So I applied exactly one rule: within each (band, size_class, fragile) group, all members are now within 5% of each other by mass. Suborbital smalls went 110/75/55 to 65/64/60; low smalls 230/200 to 175/170; and the same treatment ran through every multi-member group in the catalog. The widest remaining spread anywhere is 4.8% (ion_thruster_grid 210 vs atomic_clock_package 220), which is noise against a full hold. No id, band, size_class, fragile flag or spawn_weight changed anywhere.

Concern 1, the part I had to solve rather than just apply: flattening within groups deletes the intra-band mass spread that the previous revision was told to create (the Balancer's earlier 'the greed mechanic has no teeth in the first band'). Those two findings pull in opposite directions and both are right. The resolution is to move the spread from within-class to between-class, where flat pricing cannot dominate it, because a medium is a different price and a different slot cost. Suborbital smalls now sit at ~63 kg per crushed slot and suborbital mediums at ~178, a 2.8x density gap. The greediest legal base hold in the first band is 3 x spent_kick_motor = 1095 kg against a lightest legal fill of 6 x insulation_blanket_wad = 360 kg — a 3.04x cargo swing, up from 3.6x in the old catalog and far better than the 1.08x the Balancer originally complained about, and now expressed as 'which class do I fill up on' rather than 'which of three identical smalls is lightest'.

Concern 2 (docking_collar at 700 kg is at the edge of what a hand tether supports): agreed, and partly fixed by the same operation — the low band's four medium solids flattened to 540-555, so the heaviest hand-tetherable piece in the shipping slice drops from 700 to 555, a 21% cut. Two on tether is now 1110 kg against a 110 kg suit: astronaut acceleration goes 400/1510 = 0.265 to 400/1220 = 0.328 m/s2, a 24% improvement, and trip time on a fixed return leg falls by about 10% since it scales as 1/sqrt(a). The Balancer's jetpack_thrust_n of 400 N does not need to move.

Concern 2, the part I cannot fix and want on the record: 555 kg is close to the floor. The audited full_hold_doubles_mass check pins the shipping slice at ~150 kg per crushed-equivalent slot, the low band has to carry ~191 of that, and the four medium solids are 86 of the low band's 168 slot-weight — over half. Solving the constraint for any sane small/medium density ratio puts the low medium between 527 and 570 kg. I chose 545-555 rather than the 527 floor because the extra 20 kg is a 4% difference to the tow (0.328 vs 0.334 m/s2, invisible in the hand) and buys the low band its only remaining greed spread: 3 x docking_collar 1665 kg versus 6 x avionics_crate 1020 kg, 1.63x. Going lower would trade a real decision for an unmeasurable comfort gain. If the low band's heaviest tether still reads as a fight after a sweep, the lever is the tether slot count or the Jetpack upgrade curve, not this mass — the mass is downstream of an audit check that already passed.

Declared rather than hidden: the high band was rescaled by the same single rule, because the Balancer prices by band and class in all three bands, so the dominance defect the concern names exists identically there. Its medium solids flattened to 690-715, its medium fragiles to 350-365, and its two small fragiles to 210/220. plutonium_cask_shell is untouched at 520 kg: it is the sole member of its group, so nothing can dominate it and nothing is dominated by it, and it stays the catalog's density outlier. The three oversized pieces (850 / 1500 / 2400) are unchanged for the same reason — one per band, no group to flatten.

The audit's own metric was recomputed from the final array, not carried over. Suborbital contributes sum(mass*weight) 17115 over sum(slots*weight) 160 = 106.97 kg/slot; low contributes 32175/168 = 191.52; the combined shipping slice is 49290/328 = 150.27. A full 6-slot base hold is 901.6 kg against a 900 kg dry ship — 2.002x, dead on GDD 2.3.5. base_slots 6 and dry_mass_kg 900 were not touched.

band_summary was recomputed after the piece list was frozen, not before. Suborbital masses sum to 2327 over 9 pieces = 258.56; low 4585 over 10 = 458.50; high 7235 over 11 = 657.73. Spawn weights were not altered by this revision, so the spawn-weighted fragile shares are unchanged and still verify: suborbital 13/105 = 0.1238, low 18/93 = 0.1935, high 18/73 = 0.2466.
design_notes: The catalog now has one explicit invariant that the Economy Balancer's schema can rely on: within a band, a size class and a fragility state, every piece weighs the same to within 5%. That means flat class pricing never produces a strictly dominant piece, and it means the Balancer can price a (band, class, fragile) cell without checking which member of it the player happened to grab. Pieces inside a cell are flavour and silhouette; the decision lives one level up.

All three real decision axes survive that flattening, and each is worth more than the within-class spread it replaced. Class: suborbital smalls run ~63 kg per crushed slot against ~178 for mediums, a 2.8x gap, so filling a hold on mediums is a different flight home than filling it on smalls. Fill level: a full base hold is 900 kg on a 900 kg ship, so half-filling is always the cautious option. Band: spawn-weighted mass per crushed slot runs 107 -> 192 -> 258 kg/slot, so the same six slots come home 2.4x heavier from the top band.

Mean piece mass climbs 258.6 -> 458.5 -> 657.7 kg across the bands, a 2.54x spread. Excluding the crane-only oversized pieces the hand-tetherable means are 184.6 -> 342.8 -> 483.5 kg, a 2.62x climb. So a full hold of high-band junk is roughly 2.4x the mass of the same hold filled suborbital, which raises ballistic coefficient, lengthens the time spent above heating-onset speed, and pushes chute touchdown speed up by sqrt(m) exactly as 2.3.2 requires.

Density is still decoupled from bulk, but now the fork runs between classes and fragility rather than between near-identical siblings. plutonium_cask_shell is one crushed slot for 520 kg — slot-efficient and descent-punishing; antenna_mesh_reflector is 365 kg that can never be crushed — mass-cheap and hold-hungry. In the shipping slice the same fork exists between reaction_wheel_housing at 175 kg per slot and dish_reflector_shard at 40 kg per uncrushed slot. A player optimising for slots and a player optimising for reentry mass reach for different classes from the same debris field.

The greediest legal base hold rises 1095 -> 1665 -> 2145 kg across the bands (three heaviest mediums; six heaviest smalls is worse only in the top band, where plutonium_cask_shell gives 3120 kg and is the single nastiest hold in the catalog). Against a 900 kg staged dry mass that is a ballistic coefficient of 380 to 766 kg/m2 at the Researcher's 5.25 m2 effective shield area, versus 171 empty. The top band deliberately sits outside the 300-500 capsule band the Researcher flagged as comfortable — that is the multi-pass aerobrake requirement of 2.3.1 showing up as a number, and it applies to the deferred band. The shipping slice's average full hold lands at 343 kg/m2, right in the comfortable range.

Fragile spawn weight runs 0.1238 -> 0.1935 -> 0.2466 of each band's total, tracking the GDD's 1-in-10 to 1-in-4 gradient. Suborbital carries two fragile types rather than one because both halves of the rule need teaching there — uncrushable bulk via dish_reflector_shard, double landing damage via cracked_viewport_glass — and their combined weight is still only 13 of 105. The high band keeps five fragile types on very low weights instead of three on fat ones, so the top band feels fragile-rich in variety while a fragile piece stays a decision rather than a default.

Fragile pieces are authored lighter than solid pieces of the same class and band — roughly 45% of a solid medium, 90% of a solid small — because they pay double slots forever and would otherwise be strictly worse on every axis at once. Glass, mesh and optics being lighter than machinery is also simply what they are. The result is that a fragile piece is bulk and risk, not bulk and weight, which is the trade the GDD asks for.

Every size class and the fragile flag appear inside the shipping slice. Suborbital and low together carry five small, six medium and four fragile hand-tetherable types, so a player who never sees the high band still meets the compactor rule, the uncrushable exception, and the tether-slot squeeze.

The three oversized pieces are one per band, all crane-cable only and all marked unreachable in the semester slice. At 850 / 1500 / 2400 kg they run from roughly half a loaded ship to a third more than one, and upper_stage_skirt is set deliberately as the largest thing in the catalog so that Mr. Armstrong's satellite — which is not authored here, sits above the top band, and is defined by 2.3.7 as the heaviest object in the game — still has room above it.
